## Task-2 (10-points)

Write a function called `count_above()` that takes a numeric vector and a cutoff value and returns the number of observations greater than the cutoff. Fill in the `___` with the appropriate code to define the function accordingly. **Next to each line, make a comment of what the code is doing.** You do not have to comment lines with just parentheses. Don't forget to change the code chunk option so your rendered document executes your function!


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
count_above <- function(vec, cutoff) {  # Defines the function taking a numeric vector (vec) and threshold (cutoff)
  count <- 0                             # Initializes a counter variable at 0 

  for (i in 1:length(vec)) {             # Loops through every index position
    if (vec[i] > cutoff) {               # Check/condition
      count <- count + 1                 # Increments the counter by 1 if the condition is met
    }
  }

  return(count)                          # Returns the final count of elements above the cutoff
}
```
:::


Next, make a new code chunk to count the following: 

-- How many flowers have a sepal length greater than 6 cm in the `iris` dataset?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
count_above(iris$Sepal.Length, 6)
```

```

```

:::


61 flowers have a sepal length larger than 6cm. 

-- How many cars have a value greater than or equal to 150 `disp` in the `mtcars` dataset?

```{.r .cell-code}

      count <- count + 1                 # Increments the counter by 1 if met
```

## Task-3 (5-points)

In 1-3 sentences, explain the concept of *masking* functions.

*masking is a term used when the function name of a loaded package is exactly the same as a function name of a pre-exsisting function. This is an issue, as pre-written code may function differently if certain functions are masked to take on different functionality.*
